description: Starter fixes for scenario B, where two companies' sales teams collide after an acquisition (two Salesforce exports: deals, stage history, approvals). Vendor examples come from the analyst reports in the project (Gartner Magic Quadrant for CRM Sales Platforms 2026, ISG Buyers Guide CRM Sales 2026, Forrester Wave Revenue Marketing Platforms Q1 2026). Every price and effect size here is a placeholder to replace with quotes and evidence before a client report.

shared_customers.label: Shared customers worked by both teams

ai_deal_risk_alerts.name: AI deal-risk alerts
ai_deal_risk_alerts.how_it_solves: Predictive scoring reads stage history and activity, flags deals that have gone quiet, slipped their close date or wait on an approval, and drafts the next step for the owner
example_vendors: Agentforce Sales and Einstein pipeline insights (Salesforce)

effort.note: Medium: needs clean stage history in one place

governance.note: Medium: reads opportunity and activity data; a person decides every action
governance.data_accessed: Opportunities, stage history, activities and approvals
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
Vendor review: no training on customer data

requires.why: risk scores need at least 6 months of stage history in one place
requires.revisit: once both orgs' history sits in one place

risks: Alerts get ignored without a weekly review
Two orgs mean two data models until they are joined
ai_deal_risk_alerts.evidence: Gartner Magic Quadrant for CRM Sales Platforms (2026): deal-risk detection and predictive scoring. Price and effect are placeholders.

approval_workflow.name: One approval workflow with response targets
approval_workflow.how_it_solves: One approval matrix for both companies; discount, pricing and legal approvals route automatically, can be approved from chat, and escalate after 24 hours
example_vendors: Salesforce Advanced Approvals or Revenue Cloud

effort.note: Medium: both companies must agree one approval matrix

risks: Leaders must agree who approves what across both companies
approval_workflow.evidence: ISG Buyers Guide CRM Sales (2026): pricing coordination; Gartner MQ (2026): advanced CPQ. Price and effect are placeholders.

stage_rules_review.name: Stage exit rules and a weekly stalled-deal review
stage_rules_review.how_it_solves: Clear exit criteria for every stage, a 14-day no-activity flag, a 24-hour approval target and a 30-minute weekly review of every stalled deal
example_vendors: CRM list views and reports already licensed

effort.note: Low: one meeting and a shared list

risks: The review turns into a status read-out unless it ends in decisions
stage_rules_review.evidence: Team Tom starter estimate. Effect is a placeholder.

ai_account_matching.name: AI account matching across both CRMs
ai_account_matching.how_it_solves: Matches the same customer across both companies' records despite different names and domains, flags collisions before anyone reaches out, and suggests one owner for a person to confirm

effort.note: Medium: two customer databases to map

governance.note: Medium: reads customer records from both companies; merges need human approval
governance.data_accessed: Account and contact records from both CRMs
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
Legal clears customer-data sharing between the two companies
A person approves every merge and owner change

requires.why: the two companies' customer data can only be combined once legal clears data sharing

risks: Matching alone does not settle who owns the account
ai_account_matching.evidence: Forrester Wave Revenue Marketing Platforms Q1 2026: identity resolution and account matching. Price and effect are placeholders.

unified_account_master.name: One account master and territory rules
unified_account_master.how_it_solves: Connect or merge the two CRM orgs so every customer has one account record, one owner and one territory, with both companies' open deals visible on it
example_vendors: MuleSoft or Salesforce Connect for org-to-org sync
Org merge with a Salesforce partner

effort.note: High: two orgs, two data models and every rep's accounts

risks: Long project; collisions continue until it is live
Ownership disputes surface during the merge
unified_account_master.evidence: ISG Buyers Guide CRM Sales (2026): territory alignment. Price and effect are placeholders.

rules_of_engagement.name: Rules of engagement, a conflict desk and cross-sell training
rules_of_engagement.how_it_solves: Written rules say who owns a shared account, a referral split rewards both teams for cross-selling, a 30-minute weekly desk settles conflicts, and each team learns the other's offers
risks: Rules fail if leaders make exceptions for big accounts
rules_of_engagement.evidence: Team Tom starter estimate. Effect is a placeholder.

pair_overlaps.together_note: The workflow routes and times every approval; the weekly review deals with the stalls a workflow can't see.

pair_overlaps.overlap_note: Both surface stalled deals; the weekly review does it without new software.

pair_overlaps.together_note: The account master shows who owns what; the rules settle what a system can't.

pair_overlaps.overlap_note: Both find the same customers; the account master also fixes ownership.

pair_overlaps.together_note: Matching finds the collisions; the rules decide who keeps the account.
